comparisons.peer_summary: AMD provides CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks with AI capabilities and security features, and uses GPUs with software to power immersive gaming experiences.

NVDA details how RTX features ray tracing and DLSS for games, while AMD describes how its GPUs work together with software to power immersive gaming experiences for PCs and game consoles.

sentences.text: NVIDIA RTX features ray tracing technology for real-time, cinematic-quality rendering.
NVIDIA RTX also features deep learning super sampling, or NVIDIA DLSS, our AI technology that boosts frame rates while generating beautiful, sharp images for games.

Our GPUs, including discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services, work together with software to power immersive gaming experiences for PCs, game consoles and cloud gaming services.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Intel Arc graphics family powers immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, Intel launched the Arc B-Series based on Xe2 architecture, featuring second-generation Xe-cores that deliver 70% more performance per core and 50% better power efficiency than the Intel Arc A750.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC discuss specific GPU architectures designed to enhance rendering and AI workloads in client devices. NVDA highlights RTX features ray tracing for realistic rendering and DLSS for AI-boosted frame rates, while INTC details its Arc graphics family using the Xe2 GPU architecture, which includes second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to support immersive games and AI workloads.

sentences.text: NVIDIA RTX features ray tracing technology for real-time, cinematic-quality rendering.
NVIDIA RTX also features deep learning super sampling, or NVIDIA DLSS, our AI technology that boosts frame rates while generating beautiful, sharp images for games.

The Intel® Arc™ graphics family offers modern GPU features to power immersive games, creator applications, and AI workloads. In 2024, we launched the Intel Arc B-Series based on the latest Xe2 GPU architecture. The compute engine of the Intel Arc B-Series is our second-generation Xe-core, which delivers 70% more performance per core and is 50% more power efficient than the Intel Arc A750.

comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly position their hardware as leaders in the emerging 'AI PC' market, leveraging integrated AI capabilities. NVDA claims leadership with an installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs enabled by RTX, while INTC describes launching the Intel Core Ultra Series 1 as the first product with an integrated neural processing unit (NPU) that introduced the first AI PCs to the market.

sentences.text: With an installed base of over 100 million AI capable PCs, more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications and games, and a robust suite of development tools, RTX is already the AI PC leader.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

comparisons.peer_summary: The graphics market is driven by AI, VR/AR, and high-resolution gaming needs; the company announced GDDR7 in 2024, completing its industry-leading portfolio for AI inference on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the driver of high-performance graphics demand from AI and gaming applications. NVDA describes RTX as enhancing gaming through AI technologies like DLSS, while MU notes that the graphics market is driven by AI needs and that their GDDR6X products are incorporated into PC graphics cards for applications such as AI and gaming.

sentences.text: NVIDIA RTX also features deep learning super sampling, or NVIDIA DLSS, our AI technology that boosts frame rates while generating beautiful, sharp images for games.

Our GDDR6 and GDDR6X DRAM graphics products are incorporated into gaming consoles, PC graphics cards, and graphics processing unit-based data center solutions, which are the driving force behind applications such as AI, virtual and augmented reality, 4K and 8K gaming, and professional design.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies highlight the market shift toward AI-capable PCs in 2024. NVDA identifies itself as the AI PC leader with a massive installed base and enabled applications, while QCOM describes the launch of a new class of AI-focused PCs in 2024, citing analyst expectations for rapid adoption of AI-capable PCs.

sentences.text: With an installed base of over 100 million AI capable PCs, more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications and games, and a robust suite of development tools, RTX is already the AI PC leader.

For example, a new class of AI-focused PCs, including those powered by our Snapdragon X Series platforms, launched in 2024, allowing for increased productivity and enhanced use cases enabled by on-device AI processing at low power.
By 2027, analysts expect that at least 50% of PCs sold will be AI capable, compared to 22% of PCs in 2024 (consensus of certain third party analysts as of October 1, 2024).
